title: Adaptive congestion-aware token router for heterogeneous multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Prefill/decode workloads on heterogeneous GPU pools show suboptimal throughput and higher tail latency due to static token sharding and conservative NCCL patterns. Some GPUs become congested with long prefill batches while others are underutilized during decode. Kernel selection decisions (attention tiling and fused kernels) are currently orthogonal to token routing, so we miss opportunities to co-locate work that benefits shared kernels and KV-cache locality.

Goal: Implement an adaptive token routing layer that steers token-prefill and decode microbatches across GPUs based on short-window congestion signals, kernel compatibility hints, and NCCL overlap opportunities. We want to reduce average per-request latency, increase throughput for mixed-length workloads, and improve GPU utilization while preserving deterministic output and correctness.

Success metrics (measured on benchmark suite: mix-12k):
- 10-20% throughput increase for mixed prefill/decode workloads across 4xA100 and 2xH100 heterogeneous clusters
- 15% reduction in p95 latency for decode-heavy traffic
- No more than 2% regression in deterministic output and KV-cache hit rate

Approach:
1) Instrumentation: expose per-GPU microsecond-level congestion signals (queued tokens, compute stall time, NCCL op backlog) to the scheduler. Add kernel-compatibility tags to model variants (e.g., attention-tile-16, fused-mha-ffn).
2) Short-window routing policy: implement a token router that batches incoming requests into microbatches and assigns them to GPUs based on weighted score = alpha * congestion + beta * kernel_score + gamma * affinity, where kernel_score favors GPUs already running compatible kernels to improve kernel coalescing and reduce kernel-launch overhead.
3) NCCL overlap steering: when NCCL bandwidth is available, prefer token placements that enable larger collective calls (grouped all-reduce/all-gather) to increase NCCL efficiency; when NCCL backlog is high, reduce cross-GPU routing and favor local decode to avoid amplifying bandwidth pressure.
4) Fallbacks and determinism: implement per-request routing hints and a deterministic seeding mode to replay exact placements for reproducibility in evals. Add a canary toggle for deterministic scheduling vs. adaptive to compare outputs.
5) Attention optimization synergy: use kernel selectors to prefer attention tiled kernels that match co-located token shapes; where attention memory fits in GPU L2, bias routing to maintain KV cache locality.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Increased scheduler complexity and more control-plane telemetry; risk of higher control-loop overhead if windows are too small.
- Potential for oscillation between GPUs; mitigated by dampening and minimum residency windows.
- Slight risk of edge-case correctness regressions; will gate behind deterministic replay and automated evals.

Implementation milestones:
- M1: telemetry + kernel tags (PR + perf harness) (ETA 2 weeks)
- M2: routing policy prototype & simulator (ETA 3 weeks)
- M3: in-cluster canary (dedicated pool) + bench runs (ETA 1 week)
- M4: rollout with gradual traffic ramp + rollback policies (ETA 2 weeks)

comments: 2026-02-20 - Initial discovery: observed skewed GPU queue depths during mixed prefill/decode. Logged perf traces and small sample traces attached to the design doc.

2026-02-25 - Prototype: simple simulator shows 12% throughput uplift when grouping compatible kernels and avoiding busiest GPU for new prefill batches. Simulator code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mgpu-router-sim/pull/4
2026-03-02 - Review feedback from infra: ensure router respects reserved capacity policies for Dedicated customers and does not route across isolation boundaries. Added policy enforcement plan.
2026-03-05 - PR opened for telemetry and kernel tags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2781. CI includes microbench harness (mix-12k) with baseline comparison.

2026-03-09 - Canary run on dedicated test cluster: initial canary shows 9% throughput improvement and 18% p95 reduction for decode-heavy scenarios; observed transient oscillation when window < 30ms, increased damping to 200ms which stabilized behavior.
2026-03-10 - Next: implement NCCL backlog metric and steering, then schedule a broader canary across heterogeneous pools.
